first_plain_typing_burst_submission.interpretation: The first actual effect submission no longer pays the driver first-draw cost. Priming moves this work before measured input; startup/prewarm latency and process-global cold-driver work were not measured away.

limitations: One sequential session per code stage on one Mac, with six warmed isolated bursts per case; not a randomized significance study or cross-platform guarantee.
First bursts are separate from warmed pools. Callback intervals are classified by the later shader age: early <320 ms, late >=320 ms.
Baseline used the faulty clock, so baseline early/late buckets are not fully equivalent to the fixed-clock stages.
Copy leaves source unchanged but emits 12 particles versus Typing 24.
Native state proves backend and preference application, not composed visual smoothness or screen presentation.
First-effect driver work is primed before input; total process startup and time-to-first-usable-window were not measured.
CPU-stack attribution is pending a separate receipt; no CPU-sample hotspot conclusions are made here.
The small preview stresses substantial source and edit-related capture work, not a large multi-page SVG scene.

All seven Typing post-observations had capture in progress and no ready cache; all seven Copy post-observations had a ready cache. Separate zoom journeys must establish snapshot usability and handoff; this pacing run does not measure readiness latency.

native_snapshot_verification.scope: Settings remain enabled throughout. Pacing does not establish time-to-ready or zoom/handoff correctness; cache was ready in the subsequent unchanged-source Copy phase.
